item.title: Trump calls Iran "duplicitous" after they deny his claim talks are resuming
item.description: President Trump called Tehran "unbelievably duplicitous" on Monday after Iran dismissed his claim that talks with the U.S. were set to restart.

item.title: Powerball tickets are now selling in the United Kingdom
item.description: Andria Vidler, the CEO of Allwyn UK and The National Lottery, joins CBS News 24/7 to discuss Powerball sales beginning in the United Kingdom.

item.title: Trump administration offers few details on Iran war as frustration mounts, Hegseth blasts coverage
item.description: Frustration has grown among both Republican and Democratic lawmakers over a lack of information on the U.S.-Iran conflict. CBS News' Margaret Brennan has more.

item.title: Cornyn, Tillis back Blanche for attorney general after deal on DOJ fund
item.description: GOP Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina formally announced their support on Monday for Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general.

item.title: ICE detentions set Trump-era high in July, as immigration crackdown widens
item.description: Detentions by Immigration and Customs Enforcement set a monthly record high for the second Trump administration in July, internal agency data obtained by CBS News shows, as ICE widened its crackdown.

item.title: Oil prices slide amid confusion over Iran, concern over Japanese yen
item.description: Oil prices dropped Monday after President Trump called off an apparent strike on Iran, and then said the U.S. was starting diplomatic talks. Iran denied the claim. David Uberti, a reporter for The Wall Street Journal, has more.

item.title: ICE detentions hit Trump-era high in July, data shows
item.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detentions hit a record high during President Trump's second term, internal agency data shows. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: Stevens slams Al-Sayed for focusing on Israel, AIPAC during Senate Democratic primary
item.description: Candidates in Michigan are gearing up for Tuesday's primary races, including Democratic Senate hopefuls Haley Stevens and Abdul Al-Sayed. CBS News' Fin Gomez has more.

item.title: Cornyn, Tillis say they'll vote to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general after he rescinded fund
item.description: Republican Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis said Monday they will now vote to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general after Blanche rescinded the "anti-weaponization fund" late Sunday night.

item.title: How much interest will a $25,000 2-year CD earn if opened this August?
item.description: Locking in a 2-year CD rate now could pay off right now, especially if you're planning to make a large deposit.

item.title: Federal workers sour on government work, decrying eroding job security
item.description: Nearly two-thirds of current and retired U.S. government workers said they wouldn't re-enter public service, according to a recent survey.

item.title: What happens if a debt collector refuses to prove that you owe a debt?
item.description: Debt collectors are required to validate that a debt is legally owed, so what are the repercussions if they refuse?

item.title: Lawmakers grow frustrated with Trump amid confusion over Iran war
item.description: Iran disputed President Trump's claims that it's re-entering negotiations with the U.S. after Mr. Trump called off an apparent powerful attack. Meanwhile, lawmakers are growing frustrated by the lack of information about the conflict. CBS News' Taurean Small and Imtiaz Tyab have the latest.

item.title: Would Stevens or El-Sayed beat Mike Rogers in a Senate general election?
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate hopefuls Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed are gearing up for Tuesday's primaries. Political strategists Hyma Moore and Justin Wallin have more.

item.title: Todd Blanche rescinds "anti-weaponization fund" ahead of possible Senate confirmation
item.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinded the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization fund" ahead of his possible Senate confirmation. CBS News' Nikole Killion has the latest.

item.title: Human remains exhumed at WWII massacre site in Ukraine
item.description: It is believed that 30 to 40% of the 50 remains so far discovered at the site were children.

item.title: Fast-moving wildfires in Spokane area destroy hundreds of homes
item.description: Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown called the wildfires burning through the area the "worst natural disaster our region has faced."

item.title: How often do creditors actually win debt collection lawsuits?
item.description: Don't assume that you'll automatically lose in court if a creditor is suing you over your unpaid debt.

item.title: How U.S. officials could confirm if Iran was behind the water systems cyberattack
item.description: Lauryn Williams, the deputy director and senior fellow of the Strategic Technologies Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, joins to discuss the U.S. probe into Iran possibly targeting water systems in Michigan and Minnesota.

item.title: Investigators probe whether Iran was behind cyberattack on water systems in 7 states
item.description: Investigators are looking into whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on public water systems in at least seven states. Officials in Michigan and Minnesota say their water systems are operating safely after the attacks. CBS News cybersecurity expert and analyst Chris Krebs explains what to know.

item.title: How a community rallied around a little girl and her love for roosters
item.description: CBS News contributor David Begnaud shows how the small town of Ogunquit, Maine, rallied around a 6-year-old girl when local code enforcement officials told the girl's family to take a flock of tin roosters off their property.

item.title: Massive wildfires in Northwest cause catastrophic damage
item.description: Dangerous wildfires are tearing through the Northwest, forcing thousands of people to evacuate. The fast-moving fires have already destroyed hundreds of homes. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Paul W. Downs on historic "Hacks" Emmy run and if there could be a spinoff with Meg Stalter
item.description: Actor Paul W. Downs talks with "CBS Mornings" about the final season of "Hacks" and reveals if there could be a spinoff of the popular series. Downs also describes what it was like to tell his co-star Meg Stalter that she was nominated for an Emmy Award.

item.title: Morocco blames Ceuta border surge on misleading info spread online
item.description: Morocco is blaming a massive surge of migrants​ into Ceuta on various factors, including "malicious exploitation of digital platforms" and the spread of misleading information.

item.title: Senate pushes ahead with plan to fund government through midterms
item.description: The Senate is moving ahead with a plan to keep the government funded and avoid another shutdown before the midterm elections.

item.title: Acting attorney general issues order rescinding "anti-weaponization fund"
item.description: The order came after Republican Senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn threatened to block Blanche's confirmation for Attorney General if the fund was not rescinded in writing.

item.title: Suspect arrested in Greece after U.K. woman's body found in suitcase
item.description: Police say the suspect transported the body to an abandoned site in a suitcase and subsequently used her bank cards to withdraw money.

item.title: RFK Jr., Oz blame ACA enrollment drop on fraud, but experts cite rising costs
item.description: Rising premiums forced many people in Affordable Care Act plans to give up their coverage. But the Trump administration claims a huge drop in enrollment is almost entirely due to its fraud crackdown.

item.title: Hugging Face CEO calls hack by rogue OpenAI model "very weird and unprecedented"
item.description: An artificial intelligence model that was being tested by OpenAI went rogue and hacked the firm Hugging Face on its own, in what Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue called a "very weird and unprecedented" incident.

item.title: Flights canceled as WestJet flight attendants strike over pay dispute
item.description: WestJet canceled more than 300 flights as of early Sunday, snarling travel plans in Canada in the middle of a three-day weekend.
